1.1.1.v: आ, ऐ and औ are called वृद्धि ।
1.1.1.e: The letters आ, ऐ and  औ are called 'वृद्धि'.
1.1.1.sa: आ, ऐ, औ - एतेषां त्रयाणां 'वृद्धिः' इति संज्ञा भवति ।
1.1.1.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.2.v: अ, ए and ओ are called गुण।
1.1.2.e: The letters अ, ए and ओ are called 'गुण'.
1.1.2.sa: अ, ए, ओ - एतेषां त्रयाणां 'गुणः' इति संज्ञा भवति ।
1.1.2.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.3.v: In the absence of any special role whenever गुण or वृद्धि is enjoined about any expression by using the terms गुण or वृद्धि, it is to be understood to come in the room of the इक् (इ, उ, ऋ, लृ) of that expression.
1.1.3.e: If the words गुण or वृद्धि are used to denote the operation of  गुणादेश or वृद्धि-आदेश without specifying where such an आदेश happens, then this आदेश should be done in place of the 'इक्' letter.
1.1.3.sa: यत्र 'गुण'शब्देन गुणादेशः निर्दिश्यते उत 'वृद्धि'शब्देन वृद्ध्यादेशः निर्दिश्यते, तत्र सः आदेशः इक्-वर्णस्य स्थाने भवति ।
1.1.3.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.4.v: The गुण and वृद्धि substitutions which otherwise would have presented themselves do not take place, when such an आर्धधातुक [[3.4.114]] affix follows, which causes a portion of the root to be elided.
1.1.4.e: If a part of धातु gets removed due to an आर्धधातुक प्रत्यय, then that प्रत्यय cannot cause any  गुण or वृद्धि on the इक् letter of the remaining part of that धातु.
1.1.4.sa: यः आर्धधातुकप्रत्ययः धातोः कस्यचन अंशस्य लोपम् करोति, सः आर्धधातुकप्रत्ययः अवशिष्टस्य अंशस्य इक्-वर्णस्य गुणं वृद्धिं वा न करोति ।
1.1.4.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.5.v: And that, which otherwise would have caused गुण or वृद्धि, does not do so, when it has an indicatory क् , ग् , ङ्।
1.1.5.e: In presence of a कित्,  गित् or a ङित् प्रत्यय, any गुण or वृद्धि that might happen on an इक्-letter of an अङ्ग is prohibited.
1.1.5.sa: कित्/गित्/ङित्-प्रत्ययस्य उपस्थितौ इग्लक्षणम् गुणकार्यम् वृद्धिकार्यं च निषिध्यते ।
1.1.5.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.6.v: The गुण and वृद्धि substitutions which otherwise would have presented themselves do not however come, in the place of the vowels of दिधि 'to shine' and वेवि 'to go', and of the augment called इट् ।
1.1.6.e: The इक् letter of - (a) the verb दीधीङ्,  (b) The verb वेवीङ् , and (c) इडागम - do not undergo a गुण or a वृद्धि.
1.1.6.sa: दीधीङ्-धातोः, वेवीङ्-धातोः तथा च इडागमस्य इक्-वर्णस्य गुणवृद्धी न भवतः । यथा - दीध्यनीयः, वेव्यनीयः, भविता ।
1.1.6.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.7.v: Consonants unseparated by a vowel are called conjunct consonants.
1.1.7.e: Group of two or more  व्यञ्जनानि pronounced together without any स्वर or a pause between them is referred as संयोग.
1.1.7.sa: स्वरस्य विरामस्य च व्यवधानं विना उच्चारितानां व्यञ्जनानां समूहः 'संयोगः' नाम्ना ज्ञायते ।
1.1.7.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.8.v: That which is pronounced by the nose along with the mouth is called अनुनासिक or nasal.
1.1.8.e: A letter whose pronunciation needs the usage of nose as well as mouth is called an अनुनासिक.
1.1.8.sa: यस्य वर्णस्य उच्चारणार्थम् मुखेन सह नासिकायाः अपि प्रयोगः भवति, सः वर्णः अनुनासिकसंज्ञां प्राप्नोति ।
1.1.8.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.9.v: Those whose place of utterance and effort are equal are called सवर्ण or homogeneous letters.
1.1.9.e: Two letters are called सवर्ण of each other if their mouth-based location of pronunciation and their आभ्यन्तरप्रयत्न are same as of each other.
1.1.9.sa: ययोः वर्णयोः मुखस्थितम् उच्चारणस्थानम् आभ्यन्तरप्रयत्नश्च  समानौ स्तः तौ वर्णौ परस्परयोः 'सवर्णौ' उच्येते  ।
1.1.9.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.10.v: There is however no homogeneity between vowels and consonants, though their place and effort be equal.
1.1.10.e: A स्वर and a व्यञ्जन cannot be सवर्ण of each other.
1.1.10.sa: स्वराः तथा व्यञ्जनानि परस्पराणाम् सवर्णानि न भवन्ति  ।
1.1.10.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.11.v: A dual case affix ending in ई or ऊ or ए is called प्रगृह्य , or excepted vowels which do not admit सन्धि or conjugation.
1.1.11.e: दीर्घ-ईकारान्त, दीर्घ-ऊकारान्त and एकारान्त forms of द्विवचन are known as 'प्रगृह्य'.
1.1.11.sa: द्विवचनस्य दीर्घ-ईकारान्तम्, दीर्घ-ऊकारान्तम् तथा एकारान्तम् रूपम् 'प्रगृह्य'संज्ञकम्  भवति ।
1.1.11.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.12.v: The same letters after the म् of the pronoun अदस् are प्रगृह्य।
1.1.12.e: The forms of the अदस् word which end in मी / मू / मे are known as 'प्रगृह्य'.
1.1.12.sa: 'अदस्' शब्दस्यरूपेषु मकारात् अनन्तरम् विद्यमानस्य दीर्घ-ईकारस्य, दीर्घ-ऊकारस्य, दीर्घ-एकारस्य च 'प्रगृह्यम्' इति संज्ञा भवति ।
1.1.12.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.13.v: The affix शे (the Vedic substitute of the case-affixes) is a प्रगृह्य।
1.1.13.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.14.v: A particle [[1.4.56]] consisting of a single vowel, with the exception of the particle आङ् is प्रगृह्य।
1.1.14.e: Except for the word आङ्, all other निपाताः that contain only one स्वर (and no व्यञ्जन) are known as प्रगृह्य.
1.1.14.sa: 'आङ्' इति वर्जयित्वा अन्ये व्यञ्जनविरहिताः एकाचः निपाताः प्रगृह्यसंज्ञकाः भवन्ति ।
1.1.14.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.15.v: The final ओ of a particle is a प्रगृह्य।
1.1.15.e: All ओकारान्त निपातs are known as प्रगृह्य.
1.1.15.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.16.v: The final ओ of a vocative singular [[2.3.49]] before the word इति according to शाकल्य , in a secular or non-vedic literature is a प्रगृह्य।
1.1.16.e: According to Shakalya, the ओकार at end of the सम्बोधन-एकवचन form, when followed by the word 'इति' in a non vedic context, gets the term प्रगृह्य.
1.1.16.sa: सम्बोधन-एकवचनरूपस्य ओकारः अवैदिके 'इति' शब्दे परे शाकल्यस्य मतेन प्रगृह्यसंज्ञकः भवति ।
1.1.16.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.17.v: The particle ऊञ् before इति , according to शाकल्य is a प्रगृह्य।
1.1.17.e: According to Shakalya, the निपात 'उञ्', when followed by the word 'इति' in a non vedic context, gets the term 'प्रगृह्य'.
1.1.17.sa: 'उञ्' इति निपातः अवैदिके 'इति' शब्दे परे शाकल्यस्य मतेन प्रगृह्यसंज्ञकः भवति ।
1.1.17.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.18.v: The particle ऊँ replaces उञ in non-vedic literature and it is a प्रगृह्य in the opinion of शाकल्य।
1.1.18.e: According to Shakalya, the 'उञ्' when followed by the अवैदिक  'इति' word  gets optionally converted to प्रगृह्य ऊँ.
1.1.18.sa: 'उञ्' इति निपातस्य अवैदिके 'इति' शब्दे परे शाकल्यस्य मतेन प्रगृह्यः 'ऊँ' आदेशः विकल्पेन भवति ।
1.1.18.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.19.v: The final ई and ऊ of words giving the sense of the locative case are प्रगृह्य।
1.1.19.e: An  ईकारान्त and an ऊकारान्त word that represents the meaning of सप्तमी gets the term 'प्रगृह्य'.
1.1.19.sa: सप्तम्यर्थे प्रयुक्तः ईकारान्तः / ऊकारान्तः शब्दः प्रगृह्यसंज्ञकः भवति ।
1.1.19.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.20.v: The words having the form of दा 'to give' and धा 'to place' are called घु।
1.1.20.e: Except for the verbs दाप् and दैप्, all other verbs that are referred to as 'दारूपाः' or 'धारूपाः' are known as 'घु'.
1.1.20.sa: 'दाप्' तथा 'दैप्' एतौ धातू वर्जयित्वा अन्ये दारूपाः धारूपाः च धातवः घुसंज्ञकाः भवन्ति ।
1.1.20.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.21.v: An operation should be performed on a single letter, as upon an initial or upon a final.
1.1.21.e: If a word has a single letter, it acts as the first letter, and it also acts as the last letter.
1.1.21.sa: केवलं एकः वर्णः अस्ति चेत् सः यथा आदिवत् कार्यम् करोति, तथैव अन्तवदपि कार्यं करोति ।
1.1.21.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.22.v: The affixes तरप् and तमप् ae called घ।
1.1.22.e: The तरप् प्रत्यय and the तमप् प्रत्यय are known as 'घ'
1.1.22.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.23.v: The words बहु 'many' , गण 'class' and the words ending in the affix वतु -- यद्तदेतेभ्यः परिमाणे वतुप् [[5.2.39]] and डति -- किमः संख्यापरिमाणे डति च [[5.2.41]] are called numerals (संख्या).
1.1.23.e: The words बहु and गण, and the words ending in the वतुँप् and डति प्रत्यय are known as 'संख्या'.
1.1.23.sa: 'बहु' शब्दः, 'गण' शब्दः, 'वतुँप्' प्रत्ययान्तशब्दः, तथा च 'डति' प्रत्ययान्तशब्दः एतेषाम् 'संख्या' इति संज्ञा भवति ।
1.1.23.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.24.v: The संख्या-s having ष or न as their final are called षट्।
1.1.24.e: The षकारान्त and the नकारान्त words which are referred to as 'संख्या' are also called 'षट्'.
1.1.24.sa: षकारान्ताः संख्यासंज्ञकाः शब्दाः तथा च नकारान्ताः संख्यासंज्ञकशब्दाः 'षट्' नाम्ना ज्ञायन्ते ।
1.1.24.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.25.v: And the संख्या-s ending with the affix डति are called षट्।
1.1.25.e: The word ending in the डति प्रत्यय which is referred to as 'संख्या' is also called 'षट्'.
1.1.25.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.26.v: The affixes क्त and क्तवतु are called निष्ठा।
1.1.26.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.27.v: The words सर्व 'all' and the rest are called सर्वनाम or pronouns.
1.1.27.e: The words belonging to the सर्वादिगण are called सर्वनाम.
1.1.27.sa: सर्वादिगणे विद्यमानानाम् शब्दानाम् 'सर्वनाम' इति संज्ञा भवति ।
1.1.27.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.28.v: The above words are optionally सर्वनाम when they occur in a बहुव्रीही compound signifying direction -- दिङ्नामान्यन्तराले [[2.2.26]].
1.1.28.e: The words of सर्वादिगण in a दिशावाची बहुव्रीहि समास are optionally considered सर्वनाम.
1.1.28.sa: दिशावाचकशब्दैः निर्मितः यः बहुव्रीहिसमासः, तस्मिन् विद्यमानाः सर्वादिगणस्य शब्दाः विकल्पेन सर्वनामसंज्ञकाः भवन्ति ।
1.1.28.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.29.v: The words सर्व etc. are not सर्वनाम when they occur in a बहुव्रीही compound.
1.1.29.e: The words of सर्वादिगण, when used to create a बहुव्रीहिसमास are not called सर्वनाम.
1.1.29.sa: बहुव्रीहिसमासे कर्त्तव्ये सर्वादिगणस्य शब्दानाम्  'सर्वनाम' इति संज्ञा न भवति ।
1.1.29.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.30.v: In the Instrumental Determinative Compounds the words सर्व etc. are not सर्वनाम।
1.1.30.e: The words of the सर्वादिगण participating in a तृतीयासमास are not called सर्वनाम.
1.1.30.sa: तृतीयासमासे विद्यमानस्य सर्वादिगणस्य शब्दानाम् 'सर्वनाम' इति संज्ञा न भवति ।
1.1.30.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.31.v: And in Collective Compound -- दिङ्नामान्यन्तराले [[2.2.26]], the words सर्व etc. are not सर्वनाम।
1.1.31.e: The words formed by the द्वन्द्व समास of the words of सर्वादिगण are not called सर्वनाम.
1.1.31.sa: सर्वादिगणस्य शब्दैः द्वन्द्वसमासेन निर्मितः शब्दः सर्वनामसंज्ञकः न भवति ।
1.1.31.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.32.v: Their द्वन्द compounds are optionally सर्वनाम when the nominative plural termination जस् follows.
1.1.32.e: The words formed by the द्वन्द्व समास of the words of सर्वादिगण are optionally called सर्वनाम when they get the 'जस्' pratyay.
1.1.32.sa: सर्वादिगणस्य शब्दैः द्वन्द्वसमासेन निर्मितः शब्दः जस्-प्रत्यये परे विकल्पेन सर्वनामसंज्ञकः भवति ।
1.1.32.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.33.v: And also the words प्रथम 'first', चरम 'last', words with the affix तय -- संख्याया अवयवे तयप् [[5.2.42]], अल्प 'few', अर्ध 'half', कतिपय 'some' and नेम 'half' are optionally सर्वनाम , before the Nominative Plural termination.
1.1.33.e: The words - प्रथम, चरम, अल्प, अर्ध, कतिपय, and नेम ; and also the words ending in the 'तयप्' प्रत्यय are optionally called सर्वनाम when they get the 'जस्' प्रत्यय.
1.1.33.sa: 'प्रथम', 'चरम', 'अल्प', 'अर्ध', 'कतिपय', 'नेम' - एते शब्दाः, तथा च 'तयप्' प्रत्ययान्तशब्दाः जस्-प्रत्यये परे विकल्पेन सर्वनामसंज्ञकाः भवन्ति ।
1.1.33.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.34.v: The words पूर्व 'prior', पर 'after', अवर 'posterior', दक्षिण 'south', उत्तर 'north', अपर 'other', अधर 'inferior', when they discriminate relative position, not when they are appellatives, are optionally सर्वनाम before the affix जस्।
1.1.34.e: The words 'पूर्व', 'पर', 'अवर', 'दक्षिण', 'उत्तर', 'अपर' and 'अधर'; when used in the sense of 'limit' but not as a proper noun; are optionally called सर्वनाम when followed by the जस् प्रत्यय.
1.1.34.sa: 'पूर्व', 'पर', 'अवर', 'दक्षिण', 'उत्तर', 'अपर', 'अधर' - एते शब्दाः संज्ञाभिन्नरूपेण मर्यादाम् दर्शयितुम् प्रयुज्यन्ते चेत्  'जस्' प्रत्यये परे विकल्पेन सर्वनामसंज्ञकाः भवन्ति ।
1.1.34.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.35.v: The word स्व 'own', when it does not mean a kinsman or property is optionally सर्वनाम before the affix जस्।
1.1.35.e: The word 'स्व', when used in a meaning different than 'relatives' and 'money'  is optionally called सर्वनाम when followed by the जस् प्रत्यय.
1.1.35.sa: 'बान्धवः' तथा 'धनम्' एतौ अर्थौ विहाय अन्येषु अर्थेषु प्रयुक्तः  'स्व' शब्दः जस्-प्रत्यये परे विकल्पेन सर्वनामसंज्ञकः भवति ।
1.1.35.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.36.v: The word अन्तर always being a सर्वनाम , when meaning 'outer' or 'lower garment', is optionally so before the affix जस्।
1.1.36.e: The word  'अन्तर', when used in the meaning of 'outside a certain place' or 'undergarment', is optionally called 'सर्वनाम' when followed by the 'जस्' प्रत्यय.
1.1.36.sa: 'स्थलात् बहिः' तथा 'अन्तर्वस्त्रम्' एतयोः अर्थयोः  प्रयुक्तस्य 'अन्तर' शब्दस्य 'जस्' प्रत्यये परे विकल्पेन सर्वनामसंज्ञा भवति ।
1.1.36.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.37.v: The words स्वर् 'heaven' etc. and the particles -- निपात एकाजनाङ् [[1.4.56]], are called अव्यय or indeclinables.
1.1.37.e: The words of the स्वरादिगण and the words which are called 'निपात' are all also known as 'अव्यय'.
1.1.37.sa: स्वरादिगणस्य शब्दाः, निपातसंज्ञकाः शब्दाः च अव्ययसंज्ञकाः भवन्ति ।
1.1.37.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.38.v: And the words ending in तद्धित or secondary affixes -- तद्धिताः [[4.1.76]], which are not declined in all the cases are also अव्यय or indeclinables.
1.1.38.e: A तद्धितान्त word to which all the विभक्तिप्रत्ययाः cannot be attached is known as 'अव्यय'.
1.1.38.sa: यस्मात् तद्धितान्तशब्दात् सर्वे विभक्तिप्रत्ययाः न विधीयन्ते, तस्य 'अव्यय' इति संज्ञा भवति ।
1.1.38.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.39.v: The words formed by those कृत् or primary affixes -- कृदतिङ् [[3.1.93]], which end with a म् or in a ए , ओ , ऐ and औ are also अव्यय or indeclinables.
1.1.39.e: A word that ends in - (a) a मकारान्त कृत्-प्रत्यय,  or (b) a कृत्-प्रत्यय that ends in the एच् letter - is known as 'अव्यय'.
1.1.39.sa: मकारान्तः उत 'एच्' वर्णान्तः कृत् प्रत्ययः यस्य अन्ते विद्यते सः शब्दः 'अव्यय' नाम्ना ज्ञायते ।
1.1.39.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.40.v: The words ending in क्त्व , तोसुन् -- भावलक्षणे स्थेण्कृञ्वदिचरिहुतमिजनिभ्यस्तोसुन् [[3.4.16]], and कसुन् are अव्यय or indeclinables.
1.1.40.e: The words ending in क्त्वा, तोसुन् and कसुन् प्रत्यय are known as 'अव्यय'.
1.1.40.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.41.v: The compound called अव्ययीभाव is also अव्यय or indeclinable.
1.1.41.e: The word formed using an अव्ययीभाव समास are known as अव्यय.
1.1.41.sa: अव्ययीभावसमासेन निर्मितस्य शब्दस्य 'अव्यय' इति संज्ञा भवति ।
1.1.41.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.42.v: The affix शि [[7.1.20]] is called सर्वनामस्थान।
1.1.42.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.43.v: The first five case affixes comprised in the प्रत्यहार सुट् (i.e. the three case-terminations of the Nominative, and the singular and dual of the Accusative) are also called सर्वनामस्थान , except the case-affixes of the neuter gender.
1.1.43.e: The सुँ, औ, जस्, अम्, and औट् प्रत्ययाः attached to a non-नपुंसकलिङ्ग word are called 'सर्वनामस्थान'.
1.1.43.sa: नपुंसकलिङ्गभिन्नशब्दात् विहितानाम् 'सुँ', 'औ', 'जस्', 'अम्', 'औट्' प्रत्ययानाम् 'सर्वनामस्थान' इति संज्ञा भवति ।
1.1.43.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.44.v: May or may not' is called विभाषा or option.
1.1.44.e: The word विभाषा is used to indicate the meaning of 'optional negation' and 'optional application'.
1.1.44.sa: 'वैकल्पिकः निषेधः' तथा च 'वैकल्पिकी प्राप्तिः' एतयोः 'विभाषा' इति संज्ञा भवति ।
1.1.44.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.45.v: The इक् vowels which replace the semi-vowels यण् are called सम्प्रसारण।
1.1.45.e: An 'इक्' letter that comes as a replacement for a 'यण्' letter is known as सम्प्रसारण.
1.1.45.sa: यण्-वर्णस्य स्थाने विधीयमानः इक्-वर्णः सम्प्रसारणम् नाम्ना ज्ञायते ।
1.1.45.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.46.v: Of whatsoever the augments enunciated are distinguished by an indicatory ट् or क् , they precede or follow it accordingly.
1.1.46.e: A टित्-आगम is attached before its substrate, and a कित्-आगम comes after its substrate.
1.1.46.sa: टित्-आगमः आगमिनः आदौ विधीयते, कित्-आगमः आगमिनः अन्ते विधीयते ।
1.1.46.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.47.v: The augment that has an indicatory म् comes after the last among the vowels and becomes the final position of that which it augments.
1.1.47.e: A मित्-आगम is attached after the last स्वर of its substrate.
1.1.47.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.48.v: Of एच् vowels, इक् is the substitute, when short is to be substituted.
1.1.48.e: When an 'एच्' letter undergoes a हस्वादेश, it is replaced by an 'इक्' letter.
1.1.48.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.49.v: The force of the genitive case in a sūtra is that of the phrase 'in the place of', when no special rules qualify the sense of Genitive 6th-Case.
1.1.49.e: When the षष्ठी विभक्ति occurring in a sutra does not indicate a clear relationship,  it is considered to indicate the स्थानी.
1.1.49.sa: सूत्रेषु विद्यमानया षष्ठीविभक्त्या यत्र सम्बन्धस्य स्पष्टं ज्ञानं न भवति, तत्र षष्ठीविभक्तिः स्थानिनः (उच्चारणप्रसङ्गस्य)  निर्देशं करोति ।
1.1.49.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.50.v: When a common term is obtained as a substitute, the likest of its significates to that in the place of which it comes, is the actual substitute.
1.1.50.e: Out of multiple आदेशाः possible in a place, the one that is closest in properties gets selected.
1.1.50.sa: स्थानिनः अनेके आदेशाः सम्भवन्ति चेत् तेभ्यः सदृशतमः आदेशः एव विधीयते ।
1.1.50.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.51.v: When a letter of अण् प्रत्यहार comes as a substitute for ऋ it is always followed by र्।
1.1.51.e: Any अ, आ, इ, ई, उ, ऊ letter appearing as an आदेश in place of a ऋकार/ऌकार is always followed by the letter र्/ल् respectively.
1.1.51.sa: ऋवर्णस्य/ऌवर्णस्य आदेशरूपेण विधीयमानात् अवर्णात्/इवर्णात्/उवर्णात् अनन्तरम् नित्यम् (यथासङ्ख्यम्) रेफः / लकारः  विधीयते ।
1.1.51.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.52.v: The substitute takes the place of only the final letter (of that which is denoted by a term exhibited in the Genitive 6th-Case.
1.1.52.e: आदेश told in a sutra happens in the place of the last letter of the स्थानी.
1.1.52.sa: सूत्रेण उक्तः आदेशः स्थानिनः अन्तिमवर्णस्य स्थाने भवति ।
1.1.52.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.53.v: And the substitute which is indicatory ङ् (even though it consists of more than one letter) takes the place of the final letter only of the original expression.
1.1.53.e: A ङित्-आदेश happens to the last letter of the  स्थानी.
1.1.53.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.54.v: That which is enjoined to come in the room of what follows is to be understood as coming in the room only of the first letter thereof.
1.1.54.e: The आदेश told on the latter word of a given निमित्त happens on its first letter.
1.1.54.sa: निमित्तं निर्दिश्य तस्मात् अनन्तरं विद्यमानस्य शब्दस्य उक्तः आदेशः तस्य प्रथमवर्णस्य स्थाने विधीयते ।
1.1.54.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.55.v: A substitute consisting of more than one letter and a substitute having an indicatory श् take the place of the whole of the original expression exhibited in the Genitive 6th-Case.
1.1.55.e: An आदेश which either has more than one letters, or is शित् - replaces the entire स्थानी.
1.1.55.sa: अनेकाल् आदेशः, शित्-आदेशः च सम्पूर्णस्थानिनः  स्थाने विधीयते ।
1.1.55.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.56.v: A substitute (आदेश) is like the former occupant (स्थानी) but not in the case of a rule the occasion for the operation of which is furnished by the letters of the original term.
1.1.56.e: An आदेश acts like a स्थानी in the context of the operations that are not associated with a single letter.
1.1.56.sa: एकवर्णाश्रितानि कार्याणि विहाय अन्येषु स्थान्याश्रयेषु कार्येषु  आदेशः स्थानिवत् भवति ।
1.1.56.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.57.v: A substitute in the room of a vowel caused by something that follows, should be regarded as that whose place it takes when a rule would else take effect on what stands anterior to the original vowel.
1.1.57.e: An आदेश done in place of an अच् letter due to the परनिमित्त acts like the स्थानी even in the context of कार्याणि that are associated with a single letter; as long as the कार्याणि are on an entity prior to the location of the स्थानी.
1.1.57.sa: अच् वर्णस्य स्थाने क्रियमाणस्य आदेशस्य निमित्तम् परः अस्ति चेत् स्थानिनः पूर्वपदार्थस्य एकवर्णाश्रितेषु कार्येषु अपि सः आदेशः स्थानीवद् भवति ।
1.1.57.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.58.v: Not so, in rules relating to the finals of words, to the doubling of letters, to the affixing of वरच् , to the elision of य , to accent, to homogenous letters, to अनुस्वर , to the lengthening of vowels and to the substitution of जस् and चर् characters.
1.1.58.e: An आदेश done in place of an अच् letter due to the परनिमित्त never acts like a स्थानी; even for the single-letter-कार्याणि done on an entity prior to the location of the स्थानी; in the context of -  (1) पदान्तकार्य  (2) द्वित्वकार्य  (3) 'वरच्' प्रत्ययकार्य (4) यकारलोप  (5) स्वरविधि (6) सवर्णकार्य (7) अनुस्वारविधि (8) दीर्घादेशकार्य (9) जश्त्वकार्य and (10) चर्त्वकार्य.
1.1.58.sa: अच् वर्णस्य स्थाने क्रियमाणस्य आदेशस्य निमित्तम् परः अस्ति चेत् सः आदेशः - (1) पदान्तकार्यार्थम्  (2) द्वित्वकार्यार्थम्  (3) 'वरच्' प्रत्ययस्य कार्यार्थम् (4) यकारलोपार्थम्  (5) स्वरविध्यर्थम्    (6) सवर्णकार्यार्थम्   (7) अनुस्वारविध्यर्थम् (8) दीर्घादेशकार्यार्थम् (9) जश्त्वकार्यार्थम् (10) चर्त्वकार्यार्थम् - स्थानिवत् कार्यम् न करोति ।
1.1.58.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.59.v: Before an affix having an initial vowel, which causes reduplication, the substitute which takes the place of a vowel is like the original vowel even in form, only for the purpose of reduplication and no further.
1.1.59.e: An आदेश done in place of an अच् letter acts like a स्थानी for the द्वित्वकार्य, provided that such a द्वित्वकार्य is caused by an अजादि षनिमित्त.
1.1.59.sa: अच्-वर्णस्य स्थाने क्रियमाण: आदेशः अजादिनिमित्ते द्वित्वे कर्तव्ये स्थानिवद् भवति ।
1.1.59.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.60.v: The substitution of a blank (लोप) signifies disappearance.
1.1.60.e: non-appearance of a letter or a group of letters is called लोप.
1.1.60.sa: वर्णस्य वर्णसमूहस्य वा अदर्शनम्  'लोपः' नाम्ना ज्ञायते ।
1.1.60.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.61.v: The disappearance of an affix when it is caused by the words लुक् , श्लु or लुप् are designated by those terms respectively.
1.1.61.e: The elision of a प्रत्यय done using the specific words लुक्, श्लु and लुप् is respectively known by the terms लुक्, श्लु, लुप्.
1.1.61.sa: प्रत्ययस्य लोपः यदि 'लुक्', 'श्लु', 'लुप्' एतैः विशिष्टशब्दैः क्रियते, तर्हि तादृशस्य लोपस्य क्रमेण 'लुक्', 'श्लु', 'लुप्' इति संज्ञा दीयते ।
1.1.61.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.62.v: When elision of an affix has taken place (लोप), the affix still exerts its influence and the operations dependant upon it, take place as if it were present.
1.1.62.e: The कार्य associated with a प्रत्यय happens even when the प्रत्यय undergoes a लोप.
1.1.62.sa: प्रत्ययस्य लोपे कृते अपि प्रत्ययाश्रितं कार्यम् भवति ।
1.1.62.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.63.v: Of the base (अङ्ग), whose affix has been elided by the use of the three words containing लु , the operations dependant on it do not take place, regarding such base.
1.1.63.e: A प्रत्यय that has been removed लुक् , श्लु or लुप् does not cause any अङ्गकार्यम्.
1.1.63.sa: लुक्/श्लुः/लुप् - एतैः शब्दैः यस्य प्रत्ययस्य लोपः भवति तस्य निमित्तकम् अङ्गकार्यम्  न भवति ।
1.1.63.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.64.v: The final portion of a word, beginning with the last among the vowels in the word, is called टि।
1.1.64.e: The fragment of a word starting from its last अच् letter till the end is called टि.
1.1.64.sa: शब्दस्य अन्तिम-अच्-वर्णात् आरभ्य शब्दस्य अन्तिमवर्णं यावत् विद्यमानस्य अंशस्य 'टि' इति संज्ञा भवति ।
1.1.64.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.65.v: The letter immediately preceding the last letter of a word is called penultimate (उपधा).
1.1.65.e: The second-last letter of a word is called उपधा.
1.1.65.sa: शब्दे अन्तिमवर्णात् पूर्वम् विद्यमानस्य वर्णस्य 'उपधा' इति संज्ञा भवति ।
1.1.65.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.66.v: When a term is exhibited in the seventh case in these sūtras, the operation directed, is to be understood as effecting the state of what immediately precedes the which the term denotes.
1.1.66.e: The words in the सप्तमी विभक्ति are used to indicate that the कार्य happens on an immediately previous entity.
1.1.66.sa: सूत्रेषु सप्तमीविभक्तेः साहाय्येन यस्य शब्दस्य उल्लेखः क्रियते, तस्मात् अव्यवहितस्य पूर्वस्य कार्यम् भवति ।
1.1.66.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.67.v: An operation caused by the exhibition of a term in the Ablative 5th case, is to be understood to enjoin the substitution of something in the room of that which immediately follows the word denoted by the term.
1.1.67.e: The words in the पञ्चमी विभक्ति are used to indicate that the कार्य happens on an immediately next entity.
1.1.67.sa: सूत्रेषु पञ्चमीविभक्तेः साहाय्येन यस्य शब्दस्य उल्लेखः क्रियते, तस्मात् अव्यवहितस्य परस्य कार्यम् भवति ।
1.1.67.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.68.v: In this Grammar, when an operation is directed with regard to a word, the individual form of the word possessing meaning is to be understood, except with regard to a word which is a definition.
1.1.68.e: The words used in the rules of the grammar represent the verbatim sequence of the letters (and not their underlying meaning); except for the technical terms which represent the meaning rather than the verbatim sequence of the letters.
1.1.68.sa: व्याकरणशास्त्रे संज्ञाशब्दान् वर्जयित्वा अन्यत्र शब्दग्रहणेन स्वरूपग्रहणं भवति । संज्ञाशब्दानां ग्रहणेन तु अर्थग्रहणं क्रियते ।
1.1.68.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.69.v: The letters of the प्रत्याहार अण् i.e. the vowels and semi-vowels and a term having उ for its indicatory letter, refer to their own form as well as to their homogeneous letters, except when they are used as प्रत्यय-s or affixes.
1.1.69.e: An अण् letter which does not represent an आदेश, and an उदित letter (one of कु, चु, टु, तु, पु) used in a sutra represent all the सवर्ण forms.
1.1.69.sa: सूत्रे आदेशरूपेण न प्रयुक्तः 'अण्' वर्णः, तथा च उदित् वर्णः (कु, चु, टु, तु, पु - इति) सवर्णानाम् ग्रहणं करोति ।
1.1.69.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.70.v: The letter which has त् after or before it, besides referring to its own form, refers to those homogeneous letters which have the some prosodial length or time.
1.1.70.e: A letter that follows or is followed by 'त्' represents only those सवर्णाः which require the same time for pronunciation as that letter.
1.1.70.sa: तकारात् परः वर्णः, तथा च तकारः यस्मात् परः सः वर्णः — उभौ अपि स्वकालवाचकानाम् सवर्णानाम् एव निर्देशं कुरुतः ।
1.1.70.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.71.v: An initial letter, with a final इत् letter as a final, is the name of itself and of the intervening letters.
1.1.71.e: A beginning letter, when combined with an ending इत् letter, stands for itself and for all the letters in between.
1.1.71.sa: अन्तिम-इत्-वर्णेन सह गृहीतः आदिवर्णः तयोः मध्ये विद्यमानानाम् वर्णानाम् , स्वस्य च निर्देशं करोति ।
1.1.71.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.72.v: An injunction which is made with regard to a particular attribute, applies to words having that attribute at their end as well as to that attribute itself.
1.1.72.e: A विधि mentioned using an adjective happens in the context of that adjective, and also in context of the words which end in that adjective.
1.1.72.sa: विशेषणेन निर्दिष्टः विधिः तम् विशेषणम् स्वीकृत्य अपि भवति, तदन्तम् स्वीकृत्य अपि भवति ।
1.1.72.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.73.v: That word, among the vowels of which the first is a वृद्धि , is called वृद्धम्।
1.1.73.e: A word whose first स्वर is वृद्धि is called 'वृद्ध'.
1.1.73.sa: यस्य शब्दस्य प्रथमः स्वरः वृद्धिसंज्ञकः अस्ति तस्य शब्दस्य 'वृद्धम्' इति संज्ञा भवति ।
1.1.73.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.74.v: The words त्यद् etc. are called वृद्धम्।
1.1.74.e: The words of the त्यदादिगण are called  'वृद्ध'.
1.1.74.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation

1.1.75.v: A word that has the letters ए and ओ as the first among its vowels, gets also the designation of वृद्धम्।
1.1.75.e: A word that represent the name of an eastern country and whose first स्वर is ए or ओ is called  'वृद्ध'.
1.1.75.sa: पूर्वदिशि विद्यमानस्य देशस्य नाम्नः प्रथमस्वरः 'ए' उत 'ओ' इति अस्ति चेत् तस्य  'वृद्धम्' इति संज्ञा भवति  ।
1.1.75.m: Vasu's notes and the Sanskrit explanation
